t: 3778. Minimum Distance Excluding One Maximum Weighted Edge
o: Path cost is the total weight minus one occurrence of the maximum-weight edge on the path; minimize over all paths from 0 to n-1. In example 1 the unique path costs 2+7+7+4 minus one 7 = 13; in example 2 the direct 50000-edge path costs 0 after exclusion. The elegant reduction: for any edge e = (u,v,w), the quantity d0(u) + d1(v) - where d0/d1 are ordinary shortest-path sums from 0 and to n-1 - equals the cost of the best walk forced through e with its own weight excluded, and optimizing over all edges exactly reproduces 'exclude the path maximum'.
k: cost(P) = sum(P) - max(P) = min over edges e in P of (sum(P) - w_e), so designating the max edge is automatic.
For the optimal path P with max edge e*, sum(P) >= d0(u*) + w* + d1(v*), hence cost(P) >= d0(u*) + d1(v*).
Conversely, concatenating shortest paths through any edge e yields a walk whose cost is at most d0(u)+d1(v), so the answer equals min over edges of d0(u_e) + d1(v_e).
Two Dijkstra runs (from 0, and from n-1 on the undirected graph) plus one pass over edges finish the job.

a.i: Enumerate all simple paths with DFS and compute sum minus max for each. Exponential; only usable as a correctness baseline on tiny graphs.
s: DFS from node 0 tracking visited nodes, running sum, and running max.
On reaching n-1, relax the answer with sum - max.
a.t: O(n!) worst case - every simple path is enumerated

a.i: Run Dijkstra from 0 and from n-1 over the undirected graph to get plain shortest sums d0 and d1. By the exchange argument above, the answer is min over all edges (u,v,w) of d0[u] + d1[v] - no state augmentation needed.
s: Build undirected adjacency; Dijkstra from 0 giving d0, Dijkstra from n-1 giving d1.
For each edge (u,v,w), relax the answer with d0[u] + d1[v] (both endpoints finite).
a.t: O(E log V) - two Dijkstra runs dominate; the final edge scan is O(E)
a.sp: O(V + E) for adjacency and distance arrays

w: Prove the min-max exchange identity on the whiteboard - it converts an exotic cost into two vanilla Dijkstras. Pitfalls: treating the graph as directed (edges are undirected despite u < v in input), forgetting that ties on the maximum are irrelevant (subtracting any max occurrence gives the same value), and overflow in Java/C++ sums. Follow-up: exclude the k largest edges, or directed graphs.
